message.content: Good morning. I need your help with an email. It’s for that engineering firm where Ola wants to do her internship this summer.

content.text: Good morning, Krzysztof. I can certainly help with that. Do you have the name of the firm or the contact person?

content.text: Understood. We can keep the tone professional yet warm. To help me draft it, could you tell me a bit more about what specific skills Ola has that would be relevant to Penta Group?

message.content: Well, she has been working with structural analysis software for two years now, and she finished her thesis on sustainable concrete last month. That should be enough, right? I don't want to list every little thing she has done.

content.text: That is perfect. Those are strong points. Shall I draft the email now? I will include her name, mention the internship for the summer, and highlight her thesis on sustainable concrete and her software experience.

message.content: Yes, please do. And make sure to mention that she is my granddaughter, but keep it subtle. I don't want it to look like I am pulling strings. Just a polite introduction.

content.text: I will phrase it as a personal recommendation based on her academic achievements. Here is the draft: 'Dear Mrs. Kowalska, I am writing to recommend Ola Nowak for an internship at Penta Group this summer. I believe she would be a valuable addition to your team.' How does that sound?

message.content: It sounds good. Clear and not too pushy. Please send it to me so I can review it one last time before I hit send. I have some diabetes management to attend to after this.
